newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WINS OPENING WORLD CUP GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WINS OPENING WORLD CUP GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Katja Seizinger of Germany began her defence of the overall World Cup title with a victory in the season's opening race, a giant slalom in Soelden on Saturday.
The woman who has won every title in Alpine skiing kept her usual cool to deliver a near-perfect second run on a demanding and slippery Rettenbach piste in snowfall and foggy condtions.
The superb performance allowed Seizinger, an Olympic and world champion, to improve from second after the first descent to overall first with an aggregate time of two minutes 11.81 seconds.

Favourite and early leader Deborah Compagnoni of Italy had trouble in the upper half of the course on the Austrian glacier at over 3,000 metres altitute, and fell back to overall second in 2:11.93. Germany's Hilde Gerg was third in 2:13.84.

Although Seizinger specialises in the speed disciplines, her performance in giant slalom was impressive last winter with victories in Maribor and Lillehammmer. Nevertheless, the 24-year-old was suprised she was able to beat Compagnoni.

"I wasn't expecting this victory. Beating Compagnoni in her best discipline is an achievement. It makes me feel mentally stronger than ever and gives me a lot of confidence. Giant slalom is only my third discipline behind downhill and super-G.

"I went into this race without any pressure. I already won the overall World Cup and I don't really need to prove myself by defending it. This allows me to take all the necessary risks," said Seizinger, who has 25 victories in the World Cup of which four are now in giant slalom.

"But I don't think this victory carries that much weight for the rest of the season," she said. "We have a three-week break now before the next race (a giant slalom in Park City in the United States on November 21). Conditions are also very different in America."
The German said her main goal this season was to win a medal at the world championships in February at Sestriere, Italy.
"I have won everything already but I think it would be fun to do it all again," she said. "Although ski racing is my job, it is also my passion."
Compagnoni was disappointed victory had escaped her on the Soelden piste, flagged with 44 gates in both runs.
"I skied almost 100 percent in the first run. Then in the second run I made a lot of mistakes at the top because the piste was getting a bit sloppy.

"But now I know where I stand in relation to the others and can work on improving," said Compagnoni, a double Olympic champion who clinched gold in the giant slalom at the world championships in Spain last February.

The biggest surprise came from Spain's Ana Galindo Santolaria. The relatively unknown skier finished fourth to record her best-ever World Cup result. Her previous best was 14th at Veysonnaz, Switzerland, in 1995.
The poor weather conditions claimed many victims including Italy's Sabina Panzanini, Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, and Austrian veteran and 1993 overall World Cup winner Anita Wachter.
The first men's World Cup race, a giant slalom, will be held on the same slope in Soelden on Sunday.
